metaData.title: Atlantic Shipwrights Guild job board review

sentences.text: Morning. This is the job board review we pushed from last month, so I have kept it to thirty minutes.
Morning. Thirty is plenty, the board is a small part of what we do but it is the part people notice.
Give me the volume first. How many live listings are you carrying at the moment?
Between seventy and ninety at any point in the year, and it swings with the season.
Yards hire in late winter for the spring haul out, so February and March are busy and August is quiet.
Right now we have seventy four live, which is normal for September.
And who places them, the yards themselves or your office?
The yards place them. We give each member yard a login and they post their own vacancies.
That was the whole point of moving off the newsletter, and on the whole it has worked.
On the whole. What is the part that has not?
Listings come down when they expire and nothing tells the yard that it happened.
Nobody gets a note before a listing drops off the board, so the yard that placed it finds out only when somebody phones to ask why it disappeared.
That call comes to us rather than to them, because we are the ones whose name is on the site.
It happened four times in August alone and one of those yards had been paying for a featured slot at the time.
The featured slot makes that worse. Did you have to refund it?
We refunded half of it and they were reasonable about the rest, but I would rather not have the conversation at all.
The yard had assumed the listing was live for the full month they paid for, and from their side it simply stopped.
Let me play that back. The expiry itself is working as it should, it is the silence around it that is the problem.
Yes. If the yard got a message a few days out they would either extend it or let it go on purpose.
Instead it goes quietly and the first anyone hears is a complaint.
That is clear enough for me to take forward. I will write it up with the August examples if you can send them.
I will send the four. Two of them are from the same yard, which tells you something on its own.
Noted. While I have you, how is the apprenticeship scheme sitting alongside the board?
It is growing faster than the board is. Nineteen placements this year against eleven last year.
They are advertised in the same place but they are a different animal, because a placement runs for two years and a vacancy runs for a month.
Does that difference cause you any trouble in practice?
Not so far. We set a long date on them and check them once a quarter by eye.
The volume is low enough that a person can hold it in their head, which is a sentence I know I will regret saying one day.
I will take the expiry item away and come back to you within the week.
Send the four examples when you get a moment and I will attach them to what I write.
They will be with you this afternoon. Thanks for keeping the slot.
